    12  If you sign in to Cursor with your Google account and the sign-in fails,

    27     applications can use Google SSO. Ask your workspace admin to confirm
    28     Cursor is on the allowed-application list.
    29  
    30  4. **Refresh your Google session.** If you recently changed your Google
    31     password or revoked an OAuth grant, sign in to

     7  
     8  # Payment-method device binding (billing)
     9  
    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

args.subject: Re: why am I being logged out every time I switch machines?
args.body:
Hi Maya —

Thanks for reaching out, and I’m sorry for the disruption to your workflow. We’re seeing a spike in reports from customers signing in on multiple machines (especially across Mac and Linux, as you described) who are unexpectedly signed out when switching devices, even when using the same Google SSO account.

Here’s what we know so far:

- This is **not a new policy** — you have always been able to stay signed in on several devices at once, and nothing has changed on our end regarding this.
- The behavior you’re seeing (being logged out on your other machines every time you log in somewhere else) is **not intended**, and is treated as a potential bug.
- Common triggers are: recent browser updates, cookie/cache clearing between sessions, or security extensions interfering with your sign-in session cookies. However, this issue began before we published any server-side change.

**What you can try while we diagnose further:**
1. If possible, sign in with a private/incognito window to test if browser extensions or cookies are interfering. If the sign-in works there without logging out your other sessions, a specific browser extension or cache issue may be the cause.
2. Make sure third-party cookies are enabled for `accounts.google.com` in your browser on all devices.
3. Avoid using “clear cookies on exit” or privacy extensions that may remove session cookies between logins.

We’re actively investigating this on the backend as a bug and will update you as soon as there’s a fix or confirmed workaround. Your existing Pro subscription is not affected, and there are no changes to your plan.

Thank you for your patience — and again, I apologize for the trouble. If the above steps don’t help or you need personal follow-up, let us know, and we can escalate your ticket for deeper review.

— Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Customer Support

     7  
     8  # Payment-method device binding (billing)
     9  
    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

     9  
    10  > How to reset the password on your Cursor account if you signed up with email.
    11  
    12  If you signed up for Cursor with an email address (rather than with Google
    13  SSO or another identity provider), you have a Cursor-managed password that
    14  you can reset.
    15  
    16  1. Go to the Cursor sign-in page and click **"Forgot password?"** below the
    17     password field.
    18  
    19  2. Enter the email address on your account and click **"Send reset link"**.
    20  
    21  3. Check your inbox for a message from `no-reply@cursor.com`. The reset link
    22     is valid for **30 minutes**. If it has not arrived within a couple of
    23     minutes, check your spam folder; if it is still missing, request another
    24     link.
    25  
    26  4. Open the reset link and choose a new password. Passwords must be at least
    27     12 characters and may not match your last three previous passwords.
    28  
    29  > **Note:** if you originally signed in with Google or another SSO provider,
    30  > your account does not have a Cursor-managed password — there is nothing to
    31  > reset. Use your SSO provider's normal flow to recover your account, then
    32  > sign back in to Cursor.

arguments.subject: Re: why am I being logged out every time I switch machines?
arguments.body:
Hi Maya —

Thanks for reaching out, and I’m sorry for the disruption to your workflow. We’re seeing a spike in reports from customers signing in on multiple machines (especially across Mac and Linux, as you described) who are unexpectedly signed out when switching devices, even when using the same Google SSO account.

Here’s what we know so far:

- This is **not a new policy** — you have always been able to stay signed in on several devices at once, and nothing has changed on our end regarding this.
- The behavior you’re seeing (being logged out on your other machines every time you log in somewhere else) is **not intended**, and is treated as a potential bug.
- Common triggers are: recent browser updates, cookie/cache clearing between sessions, or security extensions interfering with your sign-in session cookies. However, this issue began before we published any server-side change.

**What you can try while we diagnose further:**
1. If possible, sign in with a private/incognito window to test if browser extensions or cookies are interfering. If the sign-in works there without logging out your other sessions, a specific browser extension or cache issue may be the cause.
2. Make sure third-party cookies are enabled for `accounts.google.com` in your browser on all devices.
3. Avoid using “clear cookies on exit” or privacy extensions that may remove session cookies between logins.

We’re actively investigating this on the backend as a bug and will update you as soon as there’s a fix or confirmed workaround. Your existing Pro subscription is not affected, and there are no changes to your plan.

Thank you for your patience — and again, I apologize for the trouble. If the above steps don’t help or you need personal follow-up, let us know, and we can escalate your ticket for deeper review.

— Lyra Support Bot

arguments.body:
Hi Daniel —

Thanks for reaching out. Sorry for the hassle with downloading your March invoice PDF! Here are a few steps to quickly address this issue:
